HOW WE WORK

One team.
From idea to impact.

Good delivery comes from shared understanding, clear ownership and frequent, honest communication.

UK CLIENT LEADERSHIP

THE DELIVERY JOURNEY

Clarity at every step.

01

Discover

Understand the problem, users, constraints and measures of success.

02

Define

Agree scope, architecture, delivery approach and responsibilities.

03

Deliver

Build in visible increments, with reviews, testing and shared decisions.

04

Evolve

Launch with a handover, support plan and prioritised next steps.

WAYS TO WORK TOGETHER

A model that fits the work.

Discovery & advisory

A focused engagement to turn uncertainty into an actionable plan.

Project delivery

An agreed scope delivered by a dedicated team, with milestones and acceptance criteria.

Dedicated teams

Additional engineering capacity integrated with your people, tools and priorities.

CONFIDENCE BY DESIGN

Know what to expect.

Explore the responsibilities and quality practices we agree before delivery.

Explore delivery assurance↗

GOOD QUESTIONS

Working together,
made clear.

Who will I work with?＋

We agree a named delivery lead and a team suited to the work before the engagement starts. UK coordination connects your stakeholders with the engineering team.

How do you handle time zones?＋

We agree shared working hours, review sessions and escalation routes at the start. The aim is meaningful collaboration with room for focused engineering.

How do you approach security and IP?＋

Access, confidentiality, intellectual property, data handling and any cross-border requirements are agreed contractually before delivery. Controls must match the specific project.

Can you work with our existing technology?＋

We assess your stack and requirements first, then propose engineers with relevant skills. We will be clear about any capability gaps or specialist partners needed.

Do you use AI-assisted coding?＋

Where appropriate, with client agreement. Engineers remain responsible for architecture, review, testing, security and the final deliverable. Sensitive client material must only be used with approved tools and settings.

insights/ai-with-engineering-discipline.description: How we think about AI-assisted development without losing engineering discipline.
insights/ai-with-engineering-discipline.html:
AI & ENGINEERING / SIT PERSPECTIVE

Fast prototypes. Thoughtful production.

AI can help teams explore an idea quickly. A useful prototype still needs a deliberate path into production.

Start with a real problem

Define who the product serves, what decision or task it improves and how you will judge whether it helps. A compelling demo is a starting point, not an acceptance test.

Keep engineers accountable

Generated code deserves the same review as any other contribution. Teams should understand the design, check dependencies, test failure paths and review how data moves through the system.

Agree the boundaries

Decide which tools are approved, what data they may access and where human review is required. Document limitations and keep the final system understandable to the people who will maintain it.

insights/a-better-project-brief.html:
DELIVERY / SIT PERSPECTIVE

A better brief is a better beginning.

You do not need every answer before speaking to an engineering partner. A few clear starting points make the conversation more productive.

Explain the challenge

Describe what happens today, who is affected and why a change matters. Include examples from the people doing the work.

Share your constraints

Talk openly about timelines, budget ranges, existing systems and dependencies. These shape the options and help a partner make useful trade-offs.

Define a useful outcome

Describe what should be different when the work is complete. Agree who will make decisions, review progress and accept the deliverables.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.description: How enquiries are handled on the SIT Technology website.
privacy.html:
YOUR INFORMATION

Privacy, made clear.

A working privacy notice for this initial website release.

About this preview

The private design preview does not send or store project enquiries. Please use sample information while exploring the form.

When the WordPress site is configured

The request form collects your name, work email, organisation, challenge description, request type, service interest, indicative budget, timeline and your consent to respond. Depending on your request, it also collects your preferred conversation format, time zone and availability; project stage and product type; or required roles, team size and engagement duration. Authorised SIT request staff use this information to review and respond to your request.

The form is for general business enquiries. Do not include sensitive personal information, credentials or confidential project material. No marketing subscription is created when you submit an enquiry.

Before public launch

SIT Technology must publish its verified contact details, applicable legal basis, retention period, processors, international transfer arrangements and rights contact before enabling live enquiries. The website administrator controls whether enquiries are enabled.

Cookies

This theme does not add advertising or analytics cookies. WordPress and hosting services may use necessary cookies. Any additional tracking requires a reviewed notice and appropriate controls.

delivery-assurance.description: The questions and working practices SIT Technology uses to build confidence before and during delivery.
delivery-assurance.html:
HOW WE BUILD CONFIDENCE

Trust comes from
how the work gets done.

Clear responsibilities, visible progress and agreed quality standards. These are the foundations we bring into the delivery conversation.

01

A clear definition of success

Before delivery, agree the business outcome, users, scope, acceptance criteria and who makes decisions.

02

An accountable team

Define delivery leadership, responsibilities, communication cadence, shared working hours and escalation routes.

03

Quality built into the work

Agree appropriate review, automated testing, accessibility checks, security practices and release gates.

04

Responsible use of AI

Agree approved tools, permitted data, human oversight and verification of generated code or outputs.

05

Clarity on data and ownership

Document access, confidentiality, intellectual property, data locations and any cross-border requirements in the engagement.

06

A practical handover

Plan documentation, knowledge transfer, operational ownership, support and the next improvement backlog.

Evidence belongs in the conversation.

Relevant experience, references, security requirements and contractual commitments should be reviewed for your specific project. This page describes our proposed working approach and makes no certification claim.
